pillars.title: Series Room Generation
pillars.header: Build a Universe, Not a Clip
pillars.body: Describe your series or YouTube channel once, and SceneFlow builds the whole world — storyline, cast, and an unlimited episode slate — with a Shared Reference Library that keeps every episode on-brand.

steps.title: Start with your concept
steps.description: Drop in a concept or a detailed description of your series or YouTube channel. SceneFlow turns it into a structured, production-ready foundation — no prompt engineering required.
steps.imagePlaceholder: New series intake — concept or channel description

steps.title: Review the SceneFlow baseline
steps.description: SceneFlow returns a professional baseline scored by Audience Resonance Analysis. Read or listen to the narrated overview, then steer it with your own direction.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Series baseline — Audience Resonance score and narrated overview

steps.title: Create unlimited episodes
steps.description: Spin up as many episodes as your story needs. Each one inherits your series DNA, so the cast, tone, and world stay consistent from episode one to the season finale.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Episode slate — unlimited episodes generated from the series arc

steps.title: Review the Reference Library
steps.description: Browse the shared Reference Library — characters, voices, wardrobe, locations, and props — created and maintained through Production Stage and reused across every episode.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Shared Reference Library — characters, voices, locations, props

steps.title: Direct the Intelligent Assistant Writer
steps.description: Reshape the series or any episode by speaking or typing your direction. The Intelligent Assistant Writer rewrites professional copy instantly — no blank page, no prompt engineering.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — voice or text direction on series and episodes

steps.title: Start production in one click
steps.description: When an episode feels right, start its production with a single click and flow straight into the guided Production Stage pipeline.
steps.imagePlaceholder: One-click start production on a selected episode

pillars.title: Blueprint Room
pillars.body: Blueprint Room is your deep film treatment — synopsis, beats, characters, tone, and style — pre-scored by Audience Resonance Analysis so you approve a story that lands before a single frame renders.

steps.title: Review the baseline Blueprint
steps.description: Open a professional baseline Blueprint with Audience Resonance Analysis built in. Read or listen to the narrated overview to hear exactly why it works.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Baseline Blueprint — treatment with Audience Resonance score

steps.title: Direct the Intelligent Assistant Writer
steps.description: Refine the synopsis, beats, characters, and more by speaking or typing your direction. The Intelligent Assistant Writer revises the treatment instantly — no prompt engineering.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — editing synopsis, beats, and characters

steps.title: Review the Reasoning
steps.description: Open the Reasoning section for a creative explanation of the current Blueprint — the story logic behind every beat and character choice.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Reasoning panel — creative explanation of the Blueprint

steps.title: Start production when ready
steps.description: Once the story sings, start production — and the entire pipeline inherits your approved creative DNA with no drift.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Open Production Stage — readiness gate from an approved blueprint

pillars.title: Production Stage
pillars.body: Production Stage runs concurrent, multi-engine generation — script, audio, frames, and video — with the Intelligent Assistant Director, the Screening Room, and multilanguage streams carrying you from approved script to a published 4K master.

steps.title: Review the baseline script
steps.description: Start from a professional baseline script with Audience Resonance Analysis. Read or listen to the narrated analysis to know what lands before you spend a credit.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Baseline script — Audience Resonance analysis and narrated overview

steps.title: Optimize scene by scene
steps.description: Use the Intelligent Assistant Writer to optimize the script scene by scene — tighten dialogue, reshape beats, and apply one-click improvements by voice or text.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — scene-by-scene script optimization

steps.title: Build the Reference Library
steps.description: Create or update the Reference Library with scripted, custom, or uploaded characters, voices, wardrobes, locations, and props. Edit reference images directly — no "slot machine" regenerations.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Reference Library — characters, voices, wardrobe, locations, props

steps.title: Generate audio
steps.description: Generate dialogue, narration, SFX, and music with Run All Agents across all scenes, Audio Agent per scene, or beat by beat — native-quality voiceover in 70+ languages.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Audio Agent — all scenes, single scene, or beat by beat

steps.title: Generate and edit frames
steps.description: Generate beat frames with Run All Agents, Stills Agent per scene, or beat by beat, then edit any frame with the Intelligent Assistant Director (IAD) — just describe the change.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Beat frames with Intelligent Assistant Director edits

steps.title: Review the animatic
steps.description: Play the full animatic — frames, dialogue, SFX, and music — in the interactive Screening Room, and share a link for feedback without exporting a file.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Screening Room — interactive animatic review and sharing

steps.title: Generate video
steps.description: Turn approved frames into motion with Video Agent per scene or beat by beat. Retake any shot with the Intelligent Assistant Director — no endless slot-machine regenerations.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Video Agent generation with IAD retakes

steps.title: Edit & stitch in the Broadcast Mixer
steps.description: Polish every scene in the Fullscreen Broadcast Mixer — 6-lane multi-track timeline (V1 Video, A0 Stem, A1 Dialogue, A2 VO, A3 SFX, A4 Score), -8 dB auto-ducking, Match-Cut Continuity Loupe, J/L-cut overlaps, 103% Ken Burns Push holds, watermark crop presets, and EBU R128 (-14 LUFS) loudness normalization.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Broadcast Mixer — 6-lane timeline, Match-Cut Loupe, VU meter, and EBU R128 loudness

steps.title: Render and review scenes
steps.description: Render your scenes in the cloud with FFmpeg transitions and loudness normalization, then review and share them through the Screening Room to lock approval before final assembly.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Rendered scenes reviewed and shared in the Screening Room

steps.title: Generate multilanguage streams
steps.description: Selectively regenerate only dialogue and in-scene signage shots while retaining unselected master shots, strip spoken English from video audio stems to preserve generated SFX and music, and align dubbed audio durations by slowing video clips up to 1.5x across 70+ markets.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Multilanguage streams — selective shot regeneration, stem separation, and elastic dub alignment

steps.title: Render final and publish
steps.description: Render the final production into a master and publish — auto-generated thumbnails, titles, and descriptions ready for your YouTube channel and beyond.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Final render and one-click publish to YouTube

animation.seriesSynopsis: In the retro-futuristic coastal city of Port Marrow, 23-year-old diagnostic technician Juniper Finch and co-op sound engineer Tobias Wu (24) face the imminent destruction of the North Quay Municipal Workshop—a worker-owned collective supporting displaced maritime laborers. The threat comes via Councilman Orville Crane, who has engineered a deliberate failure of the automated tidal surge barriers, framing it as an 'unavoidable climate event' to default lower-quay parcels, collect billions in municipal recovery bonds, and rezone the submerged district under private 'green renewal' charters. Utilizing her augmented deductive monocle despite the blinding cognitive migraines it inflicts, Juniper decodes municipal telemetry embedded in the eviction writ, pinpointing Crane's offshore auction barge at Pier 14 where the decommissioned floodgate controls and her vanished mother Eleanor's encrypted black-box ledger are being sold off. Disguised in dockers' oilskins, Juniper and Tobias infiltrate the barge's iron catwalks. In the lower hold, Chief Inspector Bram Halloway reaches his breaking point when Crane hands him an incendiary flare and orders him to burn Eleanor's original flood baseline archives and quietly ensure the whistleblowing youths drown in the slipway. Horrified by the cost of his decade-long complicity, Halloway hesitates while Juniper taps the auction feed, suffering a sensory seizure as Eleanor's decrypted voice reveals the flood is a manufactured market play. Cornered in Crane's private gallery, Juniper rejects Crane's offer to buy her silence; Tobias sacrifices his custom acoustic hardware to blow out the panoramic windows with a sonic blast. As enforcers swarm the slipway, Halloway enacts his redemption by manually locking the hydraulic blast gates from the outside, trapping himself with Crane's guards to guarantee Juniper and Tobias escape into the storm with the ledger, ready to expose the engineered deluge.

documentary.artLock: Period accuracy is the rule of the picture. A 1956 lab has period wardrobe, film grain, and the machines of that year — no flat screens, no phones. A present-day chapter looks like now. The same two witnesses, Dr. Amira Hassan and Kenji Sato, keep the same faces across every era they appear in.
documentary.logline: A five-part documentary follows intelligence — built, borrowed, and still unfinished — from the first useful machines to the question of a system smarter than its makers.
documentary.seriesSynopsis: Spanning seventy years and twelve cities across five continents, The Long Thought is a five-part, 200-minute documentary series tracing humanity’s attempt to externalize reasoning—from 1956 relay rooms in Manchester and Tokyo to contemporary foundation-model infrastructure and the governance horizon of superintelligence. Anchored by recurring on-camera witnesses Dr. Amira Hassan (Cairo/London) and Kenji Sato (Osaka/Tokyo), SceneFlow’s Historical Style Guardrails lock period-authentic lenses, wardrobe, and room geometry per decade while automatically weaving transcript-synced archival cutaways, schematics, and multi-language narration.

episode1Synopsis.title: Episode 1: The Room with the Switches (1950–1968)
episode1Synopsis.duration: 40 min (5 Chapters · Chapter 1 Live Proof: 6 min)
episode1Synopsis.logline: In post-war Manchester, Princeton, and Tokyo, a handful of mathematicians and relay engineers wire rooms the size of gymnasiums to test whether a machine can hold a rule and change its mind.
episode1Synopsis.synopsis: Episode 1 reconstructs the physical and philosophical birth of machine intelligence between 1950 and 1968. Moving between 16mm archival-grade recreations of Manchester’s Ferranti Mark 1, Tokyo’s ETL Mark III relay room, and Dartmouth’s 1956 summer study, Dr. Amira Hassan and Kenji Sato examine the artifacts their mentors left behind—showing how early researchers mistook formal logic for human common sense, yet laid the switching architecture that still governs modern compute.
episode1Synopsis.chapter1Title: Chapter 1: The Relay That Remembered (Manchester & Tokyo, 1956)
episode1Synopsis.chapter1Synopsis: Shot in locked 1956 16mm grain with zero modern artifacts, engineers in wool waistcoats trace a fault across clattering electromagnetic relays in Manchester and Tokyo, intercut with crisp 4K present-day interview plates of Amira Hassan and Kenji Sato holding original 5-hole punched tape—closing on a single toggle switch left on through the night.

episodes.title: The Room with the Switches
episodes.synopsis: Mid-century labs in Manchester, Princeton, and Tokyo. Researchers in period dress stand over machines that do one clever thing in a loud room. Amira’s teacher, on a later interview tape, describes the hope without using a single object from the future. Kenji’s uncle services a factory controller the size of a wardrobe. The chapter ends on a switch left in the on position overnight.

episodes.title: The Useful Machine
episodes.synopsis: The 1980s and 1990s. An expert system in a Nairobi hospital records room, a chip floor in Seoul, a translation office in Paris. Beige terminals, CRT glow, clothing and cars of that decade. Amira, young, watches a program suggest a diagnosis a senior clinician rejects. Kenji sees a line stop because a sensor trusted itself. Useful, and already arguing with the people beside it.

episodes.title: The Public Arrival
episodes.synopsis: The 2010s. A Lagos newsroom, a São Paulo classroom, a Berlin kitchen where a phone answers a question a child asked out loud. The model has left the lab. Amira is now the person reporters call. Kenji’s factory posts a notice that the night shift will “consult the system.” The chapter holds on faces reading a screen, not on the screen.

episodes.title: The Acceleration
episodes.synopsis: One present day, three cities. A nurse in Manila, a composer in Accra, a dock planner in Rotterdam. Each uses a system that finishes a sentence they started. The narrator counts what sped up and who was not in the room when the terms were set. Amira and Kenji, older, compare the notices on their doors. The pictures are contemporary: current dress, current streets, current light.

episodes.title: The Question Ahead
episodes.synopsis: The superintelligence horizon, told as a question rather than a prophecy. Amira and Kenji sit in a quiet archive — papers, photographs, and a machine that is not pretending to be a person. They ask what a system smarter than its makers would owe the nurse, the composer, the dock planner, and the people who never touched the switch. The series does not answer. It leaves the obligation in the room.

solutionPillars.title: Visual & Character Consistency

solutionPillars.title: Narrative Pacing & Scene Control
solutionPillars.friction: Building a film out of disconnected micro-prompts creates choppy pacing, flat emotion, and endless manual timeline editing.
solutionPillars.solution: Direct at the scene level, not the prompt level. Structure dramatic beats, camera movements, and story arcs visually before generating a single frame of video.

solutionPillars.title: Dialogue & Audio Alignment
solutionPillars.friction: Mismatched lip-sync, floating mouth movements, and detached voice tracks immediately pull viewers out of the drama.
solutionPillars.solution: Dynamic voice performance and precise lip-sync are baked directly into the video pipeline — delivering believable dialogue without external post-production passes.

solutionPillars.title: Workflow Friction & Reroll Fatigue

solutionPillars.title: Stylistic Consistency
